There is strong evidence that mTORC2 activates SGK1, but this is done by components of mTORC2 that mTORC1 does not contain. Studies that separate mTORC1 from mTORC2 established a lack of effect from mTORC1 to SGK1, e.g. rapamycin suppressed S6K but not SGK1 phosphorylation/activity, including in MCF-7 breast-cancer cells.
Intracellular mTORC2 directly phosphorylates the SGK1 hydrophobic-motif site Ser422, enabling subsequent activation by PDK1. This edge is replaced by the mTORC2_ic-> SGK1 edge.

Intracellular PDK1 phosphorylates SGK1 at Thr256 in its activation loop, producing full kinase activation after the hydrophobic-motif site (Ser422) has been phosphorylated by mTORC2. This edge is replaced by the PDK1_ic-> SGK1 edge.
